intro: The leader’s job is not to teach a mini-sermon every week. Your job is to protect the culture, keep men in the Word, ask good questions, model honesty, and help the group move from conversation to obedience.

movements.name: Abide
movements.watchFor: performance, guilt, inconsistency, and men turning disciplines into scorekeeping.
movements.doNotForce: long quiet times, emotional disclosure, or identical spiritual rhythms.

movements.name: Be Known
movements.watchFor: superficial sharing, fear, conflict avoidance, and men trying to fix each other.
movements.doNotForce: public confession, graphic detail, or immediate vulnerability.

movements.name: FOR THE KING
movements.watchFor: legalism, overwork, family frustration, purity shame, and physical challenges becoming identity.
movements.doNotForce: turning bodily stewardship into a competition, or implying that discipline earns God’s favor.

movements.name: Make Disciples
movements.watchFor: insecurity, perfectionism, and men assuming they need to know everything before investing in someone.
movements.doNotForce: men into formal leadership before they are ready, or measuring discipleship by visible results.

checkIn: Who is beginning to open up?
Who may need a one-on-one conversation?
What obedience did the group actually practice?
Who is beginning to invest in another man?

finalVision.intro: The win is not that every man completes every box. The win is that men increasingly become the kind of men who live FOR THE KING.
points: They steward their bodies, families, work, and influence.
They help those disciples make disciples.
finalVision.closing: The prayer for the ministry is simple: men who are deeply rooted in Christ, deeply known by brothers, and increasingly willing to spend their lives for the sake of the King.
